summary: Built exactly design section 5 (and 4.4 / 4.8 for the API): the four account pages (setup, login, reset, admin two-step sign-in), their page scripts, app/public/js/api.js and the auth_ keys of texts.js (66 keys: 43 titles, labels, buttons and lines, 23 auth_err_<code>; ru, kk and en, all within the public word rules). Only files of the write set were written.

The pages sit on the existing frame and styles (tokens.css, site.css, the structure of demo.html: skip link, header with language and theme, test-mode strip, main, footer with the AI disclosure). No inline style, no innerHTML, no external address; texts by data-t and textContent; none of the six existing pages links to them. api.js maps every code to auth_err_<code>, sends the CSRF header from a cached GET /api/auth/me (read again once on csrf_refused) and keeps nothing in browser storage.

The backend was not ready (only errors.js existed), so the live run used a stub of the API written from the rows of design 4.4 / 4.8 (the 23 codes of AUTH_CODES in errors.js equal the list in api.js). The pages were not run against the real routes: that is for the later steps.

changes.what: 66 new keys auth_*: page titles, headings, field labels, buttons, done lines, the two-step texts, auth_label_error, and auth_err_<code> for each of the 23 AUTH_CODES (ru, kk, en); no order_ key; lock and limit texts say the equivalent of «попробуйте позже» with no time

call(method, path, body, {reauth}) -> {ok,status,body} | {ok:false,status,code,retryAfter?}; me() caches the CSRF token; one retry after csrf_refused; a network failure -> db_unavailable; errorKey and failText; the AUTH_CODES literal; mountFrame(doc) = the start every account page repeats (texts, kk note, theme button, language switch) with say and clear for messages that keep their key and are set again on a language change

token, e-mail, name, password, language (ru, en) -> POST /api/auth/setup; 201 shows the done line and the link to login.html; every refusal shows its plain text; the password field is emptied after each answer

e-mail and password -> POST /api/auth/login; on totp_required a code field appears and the form is sent again with the code (spaces removed, upper case); 200 -> GET me, shows the name and a logout button (POST logout), and for platform_admin the link to admin-totp.html; a signed-in caller sees that view at once

reads #c= (22 base64url characters) once and clears the fragment with history.replaceState; two password fields compared in the page; POST /api/auth/reset; 200 -> link to login.html; no or malformed code -> the reset_invalid text, no form

needs me with platform_admin (else the not_found text, no forms); turn on: password -> reauth totp_enrol -> enrol -> key and address shown as text -> code -> confirm -> ten backup codes shown once with the save note; turn off: password (and a first code when the server says totp_required) -> reauth totp_off -> next code -> POST off

Pages (static): doctype, lang ru, charset, viewport, color-scheme, robots noindex, one title, icon, #test-mode and #ai-disclosure with their ru values, every data-t key exists and the static ru text equals its ru value, ids unique, every id a script uses exists, no style attribute, no on* handler, no innerHTML, no external address, none of REQ- / handoff / ORCH / decisions / Claude Code, no public page links an account page; the kk region of each page holds exactly the one kk button (the PB-6 content rule); the public-set cut on a copy leaves no kk, keeps 66 auth_ keys in the ru and en texts, and check-public over the cut is clean.

Live, one headless Chrome at a time with a fresh temporary profile, on a stub server bound to port 0 and closed at the end (ports 4780-4782 and 4790 untouched): setup (wrong token, short password, 201, language switch), login (wrong password, lock text without a duration, totp_required reveals the code field, totp_invalid, success view with name, logout and the admin link, placeholder text refilled on a language change, signed-in view on reload, logout sends the CSRF header), reset (fragment cleared at once, mismatch caught in the page with no request, 200, no code, malformed code), admin-totp (no session and non-admin show the not_found text, wrong password, enrol shows key and address, wrong code, ten codes shown once and the key cleared, turn-off in two steps, a refused turn-off returns to step 1, done), csrf_refused -> exactly one me() and one retry. Console errors other than the status lines of the deliberate refusals: 0; failed network requests: 0; static files answering >= 400: 0; the CSP of headers.js was sent with every page.

issues.text: Design 5.3 says auth_err_<code> «for each of the 21 AUTH_CODES»; section 4.8 and errors.js hold 23. All 23 have a text. Section 5.3 should read 23.
api.js also holds mountFrame (the start every page repeats) because no other new shared file is in the write set; the four page scripts would otherwise copy about 20 lines each.

Setup page: the language select offers ru and en only. A kk option inside a sai:kk region breaks the PB-6 content rule (a kk region holds exactly the one kk button), and outside a region the public build would show an unpublished language. kk stays reachable through the header button, and users.language still accepts kk.

Test edit A6 (PB-6) says each new page has «no region». Each new page carries the one sai:kk region around its kk button, as the five existing pages do (the rule «data-lang kk outside a kk region» is red otherwise, and a page without the kk button cannot switch to kk locally). TEST-DESIGNER must expect one kk region and no order region on the four, or ORCH must say the kk button is dropped from them.

Turning TOTP off takes two codes: the re-auth of totp_off needs a code when TOTP is on (4.9.7) and the step is single-use, so the POST off needs the next code from the app or a backup code. The page asks for the first code only after the server answers totp_required, and for the next code after the password is accepted. A turn-off refused with totp_invalid is a returned refusal, so its re-auth token is spent; the page drops it and the form starts again at the password.
Forms are <form method=post action=own page>: if the script does not load, a submit posts to the static page and no field ever goes into the address. Not in the design; no server rule depends on it.

login.js reads GET /api/auth/me on load; for an anonymous visitor that is one 401 (Chrome prints it as a resource line in the console; no script error). The inputs have no style of their own (site.css is outside the write set), so they look like browser defaults inside the pixel panel; a later style step can add them.

Tests expected red until TEST-DESIGNER edits them (design 12, F2): PP-1 and the PAGES list of public-pages.test.js (A8: ten .html files now), PB-6 of public-build.test.js (A6: the page-name list), the page lists of forbidden-words.test.js (A9).
